clinician.trajectory_summary: A girl presented with a 2-year history of multiple pinpoint sized wheals with surrounding erythematous flares developing immediately after contact with water, irrespective of temperature or source, lasting 30–60 min and resolving spontaneously, without systemic reactions. Physical examination showed clear skin with an absence of dermographism. A water provocation test, performed after discontinuing antihistamines, resulted in an urticarial eruption on the trunk after 20 minutes of contact with a damp cloth. Routine laboratory evaluation, including complete blood count, liver and renal function tests, urine analysis, immunoglobulins, and thyroid function tests, yielded results within normal limits, ruling out underlying abnormalities.
